title: Annotatio IV §.XXIV close: Reformed truly believe; two remaining Controversies (oral; unworthy) — stop before Annotatio V
pass_a_gloss: From these things I hope it will stand lucidly enough to the most Famous Man that the Reformed truly believe — and do not pretend to believe — that Christ’s Body and Blood are truly and substantially present in the Supper; and so he will confess not only that much moment departs from the fictitious Controversy, but also that an approach is already fortified to those remaining heads around the Christian faith of partly no, partly very slight moment, more easily to be composed. Hither also pertain the next two Protestant Controversies on the Supper that still remain to follow: One or the Prior, on the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body; the other and posterior, on the Eating of the Unworthy.
pass_b_english: §.XXIV close: the Clarissimus Man should now grant the Reformed truly believe — they do not feign — that Christ’s body and blood are truly and substantially present; the fictitious controversy loses much force.
Two Protestant Supper controversies still remain: Prior — Oral Eating of Christ’s Body; Posterior — Eating of the Unworthy. Stop before Annotatio V.
source_text: Ex hisce ut spero constabit Clarissimo Viro luculenter satis, Reformatos re verâ credere, non autem simulare se credere, Corpus & Sanguinem Christi verè & substantialiter adesse in Cœna, sicque fatebitur, non modò plurimùm momenti Controversiæ fictitiæ decedere, sed & munitum jam esse aditum ad ea quæ restant partim nullius, partim exigui admodùm momenti, circa fidem Christianam, capita, faciliùs componenda. Horsum etiam pertinent proximæ, quæ adhuc restant, de Cœna secuturæ Protestantium binæ Controversiæ: Una seu Prior, de Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali: De Manducatione Indignorum, altera atque posterior.
notes: §.XXIV close; two remaining controversies; before Annotatio V.
